diagnosis.result: Valley Ridge riding passed all six samples; the subsequent Valley Ridge venue evaluate returned six persistently invalid frames. The first GL assertion failed on venue/prepared-soil. No Arena Nord capture began.

Material Name: 
Material Type: MeshDepthMaterial

Program Info Log:

network.limit: HTTP 200 establishes recorded request status only; it does not prove GPU allocation or program creation succeeded.

interpretation.observed: All six venue states report GL 1282, identical hash 2186190277 and only 3 textures. Failures span depth, soil, metals, course furniture, bike/rider, PointsMaterial and MeshBasicMaterial; terrain-casters-off still fails. The preceding riding evaluate used the same new soil hooks and passed GL, wetness, rewind, resources and shadow controls.
interpretation.inference: Broad empty-log program invalidation with 3 textures is more consistent with a renderer/context/resource problem than a localized soil-fragment compiler error.
interpretation.causalityLimit: This run coincided with ENOSPC, but the recovered records do not establish that disk exhaustion caused the WebGL failure, identify the failed allocation, or rule out a repeatable second-renderer lifecycle defect.
interpretation.nextDiagnostic: A fresh exact 43 full-world sequence after disk recovery, retaining unchanged assertions and early per-view metrics. Root is running it. If it recurs, compare riding then venue against a fresh-context venue capture and record shader link/compile status; no additional production change is justified by this failed attempt alone.

observations: World43 reported WebGL error 1282 and ENOSPC while writing evidence.
Gameplay45 failed at menu startup; a failed-fetch UI was observed in the failure capture.
The recovered world trace shows broad program invalidation, including depth/basic/points/bike/soil materials, with only three textures in all six invalid venue samples.
attempts.causalityLimit: Disk exhaustion coincided with the failures. These records do not prove it caused either failure. A passing fresh run establishes non-recurrence in that run, not the original cause.

limits: The arm/hip lever and stroke response are explicit game calibrations, not measured biomechanics; this is a reduced braced rider coordinate, not a complete articulated-human multibody solver.
Still images validate pose/readability principles only; they do not identify friction, torque or inertia.

The full input-journal case approaches from the real gate under explicitly enabled demonstration control then hands off to player inputs. It does not establish human beginner ease or a whole manually ridden lap.
Root owns keyboard/touch/gamepad and network boundaries, full build/browser integration, and final evidence docs. Their checks are not claimed here.

measurements.scope: Complete production equipment fixture in e2e/42-motocross-bike.spec.ts, configured ANGLE SwiftShader. Not consumer GPU frame-rate measurements.
measurements.beforeSource: Prior final per-LOD fixture records in docs/production/motocross-validation-20261019.json; current HEAD MX450 high counts were also recaptured in /tmp/mx-bikerider-20261019/before/metrics.json before edits and match.

pose.scope: body -1/0/+1; seated/half/full standing; coasting/full braking; independent 0/50/100% fork and rear travel; steer -0.42/0/+0.42 rad; actual posed wrist/boot endpoints, existing authored 2 cm inset

bikeGeometry.mouldings: Closed and coherently wound triangle shells, outward FrontSide ray hits, wall separation from both sides, true open rear guard, fork bore clearance and existing upper-tube connection verified.

clearance.method: Actual production front tyre vertices cast toward front fender along the steered local fork axis at 27 combinations of independent travel and steering; sampled crown rays only, not exhaustive triangle-to-triangle collision proof.
clearance.toolNote: Vite optional HMR socket warned under sandbox; the read-only SSR geometry probe completed successfully.

independentRender.method: Direct Playwright Chromium runner calling the committed production TerrainView fixture; final fixture bundled with Vite write:false.
independentRender.note: Baseline and first-after used the same Chromium 1193 build under /tmp/motogp-browsers; that path disappeared and final used the installed cache. No FPS claims are derived from these captures.

compatibility.records: Previous records remain in their prior shared physics categories.

limits: Consumer GPU performance, high-quality full-game frame rates and subjective human ease/fun were not measured.

Browser checks used different software backends: component/world checks used SwiftShader and the final gameplay recovery used Mesa/llvmpipe. Those results do not establish a renderer-only cause for earlier stalls or certify physical hardware behavior.
The finite bracing coordinate is an explicit reduced gameplay model, not a solved articulated-human biomechanical model.
Terrain wear is material detail over the existing authoritative course. Extra shader arithmetic is not cost-free despite unchanged primitive/resource counts.
Two narrow background slivers in the isolated SX inside-berm capture exist at identical positions in the baseline course triangulation; the new shader did not create them.
Original reference capture hardware is unverified. Procedural rider/world appearance remains; no photographic or AAA parity claim.
evidenceScope: The original startingCommit, sourceSha256, build, staticChecks, unitSuite and browserChecks describe the MX feature on base 4d20731 before concurrent upstream integration. They are retained unchanged. upstreamIntegration records the separately verified MotoGP integration and final Horizon integration, including final source hashes and the final application fingerprint. No full-suite rerun is claimed after those integrations.

overlapCheck.comparison: Paths changed by base -> incoming upstream, intersected with paths changed by base -> original feature commit.

independentCheck.runtime: Node.js child process; did not import or execute vite.config.ts.
independentCheck.algorithm: Recursively collect every non-directory entry under src; append package-lock.json, index.html and vite.config.ts; sort absolute paths with JavaScript Array.sort(); feed SHA256 with the forward-slash relative path followed by NUL, then raw file bytes followed by NUL for each entry.

horizon.integration: Clean rebase; no conflict resolution or implementation edits required.
sourceReview: Main changes only the existing festival input/startup branch. MX touch-action typing remains present, and the normal race input branch is unchanged.
OpenWorldSimulation receives activity/spawn/result changes away from the MX riderLean normalization hunk; both sets of edits are retained.

Other incoming source changes are confined to the festival session, open-world worker/UI, and open-world car/road rendering. Standard race-worker, DirtBikeModel, motocross soil, and motocross solver paths are unchanged.
